chunks: From Abdullah ibn Muskān from Ḥumrān ibn Aʿyān who said:

I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) and he said to me, 'With what have you professed the Ḥajj pilgrimage?' I said, 'With the ʿUmrah.' He said to me, 'So did you not profess the Ḥajj and intend the Mutʿah (temporary combination), so your ʿUmrah became Kūfī (independent) and your Ḥajj became Makki (independent)? And if you had intended the Mutʿah and professed the Ḥajj, then your ʿUmrah and your Ḥajj would both have been Kūfī.'

So what he (peace be upon him) meant by this was for the one who professes the independent ʿUmrah, the 'troubled' (or single) one, rather than the one with whom one performs Mutʿah. And if it were the one with whom one performs Mutʿah, it would not be an independent Makki Ḥajj, but rather his Ḥajj and his ʿUmrah would both be Kūfī, according to what he mentioned by his saying, 'And if you had intended the Mutʿah.' And whoever professes the Ḥajj independently and does not intend the Mutʿah, it is permissible for him to annul that after his Tawāf and Saʿy, and to shorten (his prayer) and then enter into the Ihram for the Ḥajj after that. This was narrated.

key_terms.سَعْيِهِ: His Saʿy (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.ٱلْمُتْعَةَ: Mutʿah (temporary combination of ʿUmrah and Ḥajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between independent ʿUmrah and Mutʿah ʿUmrah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Bāqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the jurisprudential distinction between ʿUmrat al-Mufradah and ʿUmrat al-Tamattuʾ, noting that failing to intend the combination renders the ʿUmrah 'Kūfī' (independent) and the subsequent Ḥajj 'Makki' (independent). This narration highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh, allowing a pilgrim who initially entered Ihram for independent ʿUmrah to annul it after completing its rites and subsequently enter Ihram for Ḥajj, thereby converting the pilgrimage into the more meritorious Mutʿah form.
